Shift each subject's dates by a random offset

Source: R/anon_subject.R
anon_subject_dates.Rd

Gives every subject one random offset, in whole days, and shifts all of that subject's dates in every dataset by it. Intervals within a subject (time since dose, study days, visit windows) are unchanged, while calendar dates no longer line up between subjects or with real dates. This is the "date offsetting" technique described in EMA's Anonymisation Report Form Instructions: a random offset, with the same offset applied to all dates for each participant.

Usage

anon_subject_dates(
  data,
  key = "USUBJID",
  vars = NULL,
  max_days = 365,
  min_days = 30,
  partial = c("shift", "remove"),
  keep_secrets = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  other_attributes = c("rewrite", "drop")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, a named list of data frames linked by key, or the result of an earlier step such as anon_subject_dates(). Data frames nested in them are de-identified too (see "Nested data" in Details). In datasets without the key column, at the top or in nested data, the values are left unchanged; keys in their attributes and names are rewritten (see Details).

key

Name of the subject identifier column.

vars

Names of date columns to shift. By default, every character or factor column whose name ends in DTC (any case; ISO 8601 dates, as in SDTM) and every Date, POSIXct or POSIXlt column, in each dataset whose rows have subjects and in nested data frames with a subject (see "Nested data" in anon_subject_ids()); a list column holding Date, POSIXct or POSIXlt values counts as a Date column. vars names columns at every depth of nested data. In SDTM supplemental qualifier datasets (with QNAM and QVAL), QVAL values that are ISO 8601 dates with more than a bare year are shifted too (year-only values are left alone because they can't be told apart from numbers; a warning names the columns where they were kept). In columns not named *DTC, such as QVAL or a result column given in vars, only the values that are dates are shifted and other values are kept; bare four-digit numbers are kept too (with a warning), unless every value of the column, in every dataset, is a bare year (such as a column of birth years). Columns given in vars must be Date, POSIXct, or character or factor columns of ISO 8601 dates.

max_days, min_days

Each subject's offset is drawn uniformly from the whole numbers between min_days and max_days days, earlier or later. Defaults 30 and 365; max_days can be at most 3650. A warning is given when the range is so narrow, or includes 0, that offsets are easy to guess or some subjects keep their real dates.

partial

How to handle partial ISO 8601 dates in character columns: "shift" (default) or "remove" (replace them with the column's missing value). With "shift", a year-and-month date ("2014-03", or SDTM "2014-03--T08:00" with the time kept) moves the middle of the month by the subject's offset and keeps month precision; a year-only date ("2014", or SDTM "2014---15" with the day kept) moves by whole years, at least one, in the direction of the offset, so the real year is never kept. Both ends of an interval ("2014-01-02/2014-01-05") are shifted.

keep_secrets

Logical. If TRUE, keep each subject's offset; read it with anon_secrets(). Default FALSE.

seed

Optional seed for the random assignment, for reproducible tests. Anyone with the seed and the original data can rebuild the mapping, so do not set it for data you share. The global random number state is restored afterwards.

other_attributes

What to do with attributes beyond the core ones (variable and dataset labels, comments, haven value labels and user-defined missing values, and names, which are always rewritten): custom text attributes, list- and data frame-valued attributes, Date or factor values held in attributes, and attributes of attributes. "rewrite" (default) rewrites what it can find in them, at any depth, as a best effort. "drop" removes them, and is the strict choice: nothing can hide in an attribute that is gone. Structural attributes are never dropped, and are structural only on the classes that use them: class, names, row.names, dim and dimnames on anything; levels and contrasts on factors; tzone on date-times; units on difftime and units objects; tsp on time series; type and states on survival::Surv objects; ptype on vctrs objects (its text is still rewritten); groups on grouped and rowwise tibbles; sorted, index and .internal.selfref on data.tables; SAS, SPSS and Stata formats, and a numeric display_width, on vectors. Elsewhere an attribute with one of these names is text (for example free-text units on a number). The log counts the attributes dropped in each dataset.

Value

An object of class "anon_deid_step", as for anon_subject_ids().

Details

Full ISO 8601 dates move by exactly the subject's offset and keep their format and any time part. Date columns keep their type, and POSIXct and POSIXlt columns keep their type, time zone and clock time (the calendar date moves, so a shift across a daylight saving change keeps 08:00 at 08:00). Column attributes such as variable labels are kept, with the dates in them replaced by "[DATE]" (see below); value labels (haven labels) are dropped from shifted columns, and haven user-defined missing values (na_values, na_range) in the key and date columns become plain missing values. A clock time that doesn't exist on the new date (inside a daylight saving gap) moves forward by the gap. Study day variables (--DY) are not changed and stay consistent with the shifted full dates, because each subject's dates all move together.

Dates can't be tied to one subject's offset in text that describes the data, so there they are replaced with "[DATE]" (the default date replacement of nlp_default_replacements()): in every dataset, in the same attributes and names that anon_subject_ids() rewrites keys in (character attributes at any depth, vector names and dimnames, value labels and user-defined missing values under the same rule, column, row and dataset names), and in this and earlier steps' logs and settings, with other_attributes as described there. Date and date-time values held in attributes (Date, POSIXct, POSIXlt) become the text "[DATE]" (zero-length ones, such as a vctrs prototype, hold no date and are left alone), and a factor held in an attribute whose levels now read the same becomes text rather than have its levels merged. Value labels whose codes become equal are merged as described there. The forms replaced are those found inside text by the warning described below: ISO 8601 full and year-and-month dates, SDTM partial dates ("2014-01--T08:00" becomes "[DATE]T08:00", and "2014---15"), and dates with a month name or as numbers with separators. The log has one row per dataset with such replacements, with counts. Values in the data are not changed by this rule.

Dates in nested data move by the offset of the subject their row belongs to (see "Nested data" in anon_subject_ids()), with the same rules, and so do Date and date-time values held in list columns, at any depth through plain lists. Text values in list columns are not shifted. Objects that can't be de-identified, such as fitted models, recipes and resampling splits, are named in a warning: de-identify the raw data first, and build them on the de-identified copy.

Year-and-month dates are shifted from the middle of the month, and year-only dates by whole years, so the order between a partial date and a full date of the same subject can change (for example a start month can end up after an end date).

Dates in rows without a key cannot be tied to a subject's offset and are removed, with a warning. In *DTC columns, values that are not recognised ISO 8601 dates, or whose year would fall outside 0001-9999, are removed with a warning; this includes a month and day without a year ("--12-15"). Time-only values ("-----T07:15") and durations ("P1D") have no date and are kept. Text columns given in vars must contain at least one recognised date. In datasets without the key column (for example trial-level domains such as TS, TV and TA) the values are left unchanged (dates in their attributes and names are replaced as above), and they are listed in the log; their real trial dates can narrow down subjects' offsets. A warning lists any other column in a keyed dataset that holds dates but was not shifted: Date or POSIXct columns left out of vars, numeric columns with a SAS date format (in a separate warning; convert them to Date or POSIXct to shift them), and text columns with ISO 8601 dates as whole values, or dates inside text (which can't be shifted) written as ISO 8601, with a month name (05JAN2014, UNK-JAN-2014, 5 Jan 2014, Jan 5, 2014, JAN2014) or as numbers with separators (01/05/2014, 1/5/14, 01.05.2014, 2014/01/05), including the values kept in mixed columns such as QVAL, list columns (the text values their elements hold) and the columns of nested data frames. Other formats, such as 20140105, 2014.01.05, 2014-1-5, Jan-05-2014, 12/2014 and a month and day without a year (--12-15), are not detected, nor replaced in attributes and names. It also lists any dataset without key that has such columns or a column named like key in another case.

Text that isn't valid UTF-8 (such as a stray Windows-1252 byte) is searched through a repaired copy with the invalid bytes shown as hex (e.g. "<92>"); where something is rewritten, the repaired text is written back. A pattern that matches digits can match inside such a marker. Both steps warn about text marked as "bytes", which can't be searched, in values, attributes and names: they count distinct texts and name the columns, or datasets ("(list)" for attributes of the list of datasets and dataset names), holding it. Convert it to UTF-8 (for example with iconv()) and run the step again. Every location printed in the steps' warnings and errors has keys and dates rewritten and unprintable bytes escaped ("<e9>"): this step shows original keys as "[KEY]". It names the columns inside nested data by position (dataset.column[2], dataset.column[[]][2]), in warnings and in the log, so that a column is named the same way whether or not anon_subject_ids(), which rewrites keys in nested names, ran first.

Random numbers come from R's random number generator; see anon_subject_ids(). Run this before or after anon_subject_ids(); each subject keeps one offset either way. Under HIPAA, HHS does not address date shifting directly, but Safe Harbor removes all elements of dates except the year, so shifted dates do not meet it; see the package README.

Examples

data <- list(
  dm = data.frame(USUBJID = c("a", "b"), RFSTDTC = c("2014-01-02", "2013-07-19")),
  pc = data.frame(USUBJID = c("a", "a", "b"),
                  PCDTC = c("2014-01-02T08:00", "2014-01-03T09:30", "2013-07-19T08:00"))
)
anon_subject_dates(data)$data
#> $dm
#>   USUBJID    RFSTDTC
#> 1       a 2013-08-02
#> 2       b 2013-10-19
#> 
#> $pc
#>   USUBJID            PCDTC
#> 1       a 2013-08-02T08:00
#> 2       a 2013-08-03T09:30
#> 3       b 2013-10-19T08:00
#>
